We demonstrate the weighted sum-of-squares construction numerically by solving the associated semidefinite program and recovering the exact ground-state energy of a Richardson Hamiltonian in the three-fermion sector. We further prove that higher-degree particle-number multipliers are unnecessary when the full sum-of-squares generating algebra is used.

title: Resonant enhancement of Raman scattering in a MoS$_2$ nanotube
abstract: The whispering-gallery modes confined in the wall of a multiwall MoS$_2$ nanotube resonantly enhance the spontaneous Raman scattering by its own optical phonons. The enhancement is doubly resonant --- pump and Stokes waves hit two adjacent modes at one pump energy, and the signal scales as $(Q_{\rm pump}Q_{\rm sc})^2$ - whenever a phonon energy matches the free spectral range of the mode ladder. Near the A exciton the excitonic dispersion compresses the ladder and sweeps its spacing through all intralayer phonon energies of MoS$_2$, so the match, reached for $A_{1g}$ at $E_{\rm pump}=1551$~meV, requires no geometric tuning. A missed match splits the excitation peak into a pump- and a scattered-resonant doublet whose splitting measures the residual detuning. Selection rules confine the double resonance to the TM$\to$TM channel and exclude $E_{1g}$.

title: Enabling large language model agents for high-fidelity many-body perturbation theory calculations
abstract: Many-body perturbation theory (MBPT) methods, including the GW approximation, the GW plus Bethe-Salpeter equation (GW-BSE) method, and GW perturbation theory (GWPT), among others, provide accurate first-principles descriptions of excited-state properties and multiparticle interactions of materials. However, their use remains limited due to complex multi-software workflows, interdependent physical parameters, and substantial theoretical expertise. Large language model (LLM) agents, which couple a language model to software tools, show potential in automating computational tasks, but MBPT remains an unaddressed challenge. We show that LLM agents tested in our work, including frontier models such as Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5, do not reliably construct MBPT workflows in one attempt, suggesting that correct setup requires expert knowledge and consistency that current models lack. Across tested model-harness combinations, out-of-the-box agents average 54%, 36%, and 19% on GW, GW-BSE, and GWPT workflow benchmarks, with strong model dependence and large run-to-run variation. Errors typically originate from cross-stage inconsistencies that surface only several stages after they are introduced. We therefore develop AI-Donkey, an agentic framework that combines expert-curated knowledge with deterministic execution to enable high-fidelity GW, GW-BSE, and GWPT calculations and analyses. With AI-Donkey, all tested agents, from frontier proprietary models to open-weight models, produce complete, runnable MBPT workflows with no observed run-to-run variation. We further demonstrate autonomous calculations and post-processing on 1D, 2D, and bulk materials, including the many-body enhancement of Fröhlich electron-phonon coupling in polar semiconductors. Our approach provides a general framework for knowledge engineering to enable reliable agentic workflows in computational materials science.

title: Dual role of the RIG-I 2CARD as a signaling module and a brake on dsRNA translocation
abstract: RIG-I is an innate immune receptor for viral double-stranded RNA (dsRNA). Upon binding dsRNA, RIG-I nucleates MAVS filaments through its two caspase activation and recruitment domains (2CARD). However, how the 2CARD behaves during activation has remained unclear. Using high-speed atomic force microscopy, we visualized the 2CARD in full-length RIG-I across its apo, dsRNA-bound, translocating, multimeric, and polyubiquitin-bound states. Protrusions consistent with the 2CARD appeared only transiently in the apo state, whereas a mobile 2CARD emerged upon RNA binding. During ATP-driven translocation, wild-type RIG-I moved approximately twofold slower and showed more frequent pauses and multimers than RIG-I {Delta}2CARD. Within multimers, 2CARDs formed a complex that polyubiquitin stabilized into larger, dsRNA-deforming assemblies. These findings reveal the 2CARD as a brake on the RIG-I motor, beyond signaling.

title: Sorption Molecular Dynamics of Point Defects in 2D Materials with a Machine Learning Potential
abstract: Defect engineering is a crucial tool for tuning and tailoring the properties of two-dimensional (2D) materials. A key challenge is identifying which defects are kinetically stable at room temperature and sufficiently promising to warrant further investigation. However, identifying stable defects with suitable properties using first-principles calculations, such as density functional theory (DFT) is computationally demanding, effectively limiting the scope of high-throughput studies. In this work, we investigate whether the machine learning interatomic potential MACE can reproduce sorption trends (adsorption vs. absorption) previously obtained from high-throughput DFT calculations and extend the analysis to elevated temperatures. A total of 17,624 defect structures from the ADAQ database are simulated using MACE-accelerated molecular dynamics (MD) at both 0 K and 300 K. The results show that MACE successfully reproduces the overall sorption trends observed in DFT calculations at 0 K at a fraction of the computational cost. Simulations performed at 300 K further indicate that the qualitative sorption trends remain largely the same when including finite-temperature effects. These findings demonstrate that MACE-driven MD can be used as an effective high-throughput prescreening tool for defect-related studies in 2D materials, specially related to sorption. While conventional first-principles methods, such as DFT, remain necessary for accurate and quantitative validation, the use of MLIPs enables MD simulations of finite-temperature defect behavior at a fraction of the computational cost of DFT-based MD.

title: Transverse magneto-gyrotropy driven by spin-induced ferroaxiality
abstract: Photon chirality is inherently sensitive to structural handedness and magnetism, which break spatial inversion and time-reversal symmetries, respectively. Ferroaxial order, by contrast, hosts two-dimensional chirality while preserving both symmetries, thereby precluding its direct coupling to photon chirality. Intertwining ferroaxiality with magnetic order, however, may lift such constraints and enable unconventional coupling to photon chirality. Nevertheless, the optical response arising from such intertwined order has yet to be demonstrated experimentally. Here, we demonstrate transverse magneto-gyrotropy arising from spin-driven ferroaxiality in the Weyl magnet EuCd2Sb2. Whereas the conventional polar magneto-optical Kerr effect is governed by magnetization parallel to the light-propagation direction, we observe a gyrotropic response associated with magnetization transverse to the light-propagation direction. The optical rotation exhibits a characteristic 120-degree periodicity upon rotation of the in-plane magnetic field, reflecting the threefold symmetry of the emergent ferroaxial state and revealing the ferroaxial origin of the transverse gyrotropic response. This coupling to photon chirality enables vectorial control of the gyrotropic response through the magnetic field direction. Our findings establish an interaction between photon chirality and transverse magnetization enabled by intertwined ferroaxial and magnetic orders, demonstrating a novel form of multiferroicity with functional light-matter interaction.

title: ChemArgus: Automated Scientific Diagnostics for Lab-Grade Multimodal Chemistry Reasoning: A Frontier Benchmark
abstract: Chemistry evaluation has moved past multiple-choice probes toward open-ended expert problems, yet the benchmarks that define the current frontier still score answer endpoints alone. Such scoring conflates memorized facts with stepwise derivation, treats visual and textual inputs as interchangeable, and confounds long-horizon planning with stepwise execution. These blind spots prevent any diagnosis of where the reasoning chain breaks in a model. We present ChemArgus, a competition-level chemistry benchmark drawn from chemistry competition material, textbooks, and research papers, whose scoring replaces the answer endpoint with three measurement properties. Fine-grained scoring grades every subquestion point by point with partial credit, so a score lands at the level of the step rather than the outcome. Multimodal capability is priced on every problem containing a real image, paired with a controlled text description, so visual understanding is measured against text on identical tasks. Diagnostic attribution reads paired metrics that share one scoring unit and differ only in context construction, so a gap between two scores isolates a single cause, namely integration, propagation, or local reasoning. GPT-5.6-Sol scores 23.2% on unassisted whole-problem solving against 28.8% and 30.4% under the two sequential metrics, a gap measuring the integration burden. Through rubric partial credit and these cause-isolating score gaps, ChemArgus shows not only whether a model answers chemistry correctly but where its reasoning chain fails, so that every score it reports doubles as a diagnosis, a readout of the chain rather than a verdict, aiming to guide language models step by step on their path toward chemistry expertise, one corrected step at a time, each step priced by the rubric, point by point.

title: RGLStab: A Robust Online Video Stabilization Framework Based on Grid Flow and LSTM
abstract: The video sequences captured by aircraft cameras are often affected by external environmental disturbances. The traditional feature point stabilization methods often encounter situations where feature tracking fails and matching becomes unstable; while the existing deep learning-based depth stabilization methods based on optical flow can handle complex jitter, they have high computational costs and are prone to introducing local distortions.

title: Programming Targeted Immune Cell Migration Using Orthogonal Chemokine-Receptor Pairs
abstract: Chemokines orchestrate the migration of immune cells throughout the body, but harnessing chemokine signaling to engineer targeted cell trafficking is challenging because of their overlapping interactions and broad expression patterns. Here we used structure-guided protein design to engineer orthogonal chemokine-receptor pairs with minimal crosstalk to native systems. T cells engineered with an ortho-receptor selectively infiltrated tissues producing the ortho-chemokine, in vitro and in vivo.

title: Chemical foundation models reveal molecular principles underlying glycobiology
abstract: Glycans encode biological specificity through branching, linkage and stereochemical diversity, and have traditionally been modelled using specialised computational representations distinct from those developed for general chemistry. It remains unclear to what extent representations learned from general molecular chemistry capture the molecular principles of glycobiology. Here, we systematically evaluate the transfer of chemical foundation models to glycobiology using standardized benchmarks spanning taxonomy, immunogenicity, glycosylation type and protein-glycan interactions. We show that atom-level representations learned from general chemistry encode biologically meaningful molecular organization, providing particularly strong performance for molecular recognition, including immunogenicity and protein-glycan interaction prediction. Fine-tuning reorganizes these representations into latent spaces aligned with glycan architecture, glycosylation programmes and molecular recognition. Mechanistic analyses identify stereochemistry as an important determinant of successful transfer, while tokenization, context length and conformer generation influence the representation of large, branched glycans. These representations generalize from natural glycans to synthetic glycomimetics and recover experimentally validated stereochemistry-dependent glycan-lectin recognition. Together, our findings demonstrate that molecular principles learned from general chemistry are sufficient to capture fundamental features of glycobiology. They position glycans as a specialised region of chemical space and chemical foundation models as a broadly applicable framework for glycan function prediction, molecular recognition and glycomimetic discovery.

title: HEM-Med: A Hierarchical Agentic Memory Framework for Safe Multi-Center Medication Recommendation
abstract: Medication recommendation (MR) is critical for clinical decision support. While existing MR methods are mostly designed for single-center learning, where only one independent hospital is involved, multi-center MR with hospitals of different scales has become increasingly demanding in practice. In multi center settings, abundant data from large medical centers can improve recommendation performance for low-resource centers. Despite a few preliminary attempts on this task, two critical gaps remain. Gap 1: Existing multi-center methods fail to disentangle transferable cross-hospital clinical experience from hospital-specific prescribing patterns, limiting clinical feasibility and physician acceptance. Gap 2: They commonly overlook multi label safety constraints of MR, including drug-drug interaction risks and local formulary feasibility, which are essential for safe real-world deployment. To address these gaps, we propose HEM-Med, a novel hierarchical agentic memory framework for multi-center MR. To address Gap 1, we design a disentangled hierarchical memory module that builds patient-level medication context attribution records and disentangles them into cross hospital experience memory and hospital-specific residual memory. To address Gap 2, we introduce a safety-aware medication set generation module, which integrates dual-level experience retrieval with safety-aware set decoding to produce clinically relevant, safer, and locally adaptive medication recommendations. Experiments on a real-world multi-center eICU dataset show that HEM-Med outperforms representative transfer learning, LLM-based, and MR baselines in terms of both recommendation accuracy and safety.

title: Access Rate-Dependent Endurance Behavior of Ferroelectric Hafnium Zirconium Oxide Capacitors
abstract: Fluorite-structured ferroelectrics, such as hafnium zirconium oxide ($Hf_{1-x}Zr_{x}O_{2}$), are among the most promising materials for developing the next generation of low-power nonvolatile memories. Emulating realistic operating scenarios for ferroelectric memories requires performing access rate-dependent endurance tests. The access rate-dependent reduction of the switched polarization cannot be described as a mere superposition of fatigue and imprint effects, which are observed in conventional endurance and retention tests, respectively. The interplay between these degradation mechanisms and its correlation with the delay time in between the programming pulses remains unclear. Combining electrical testing through voltage pulses with ab initio and drift-diffusion simulations provides a comprehensive perspective on the microscopic origin of the access rate-dependent reduction of the switched polarization of ferroelectric capacitors based on product-relevant 5 nm thick $Hf_{0.5}Zr_{0.5}O_{2}$ films. The role of oxygen vacancy defects accumulating at the electrode-ferroelectric interface with delay time in reducing the fraction of switchable domains is elucidated considering electron transfer processes which change the defect charge state. Building upon this theoretical understanding, a physics-based model to extrapolate the long-term access rate-dependent endurance performance is developed and experimentally verified for temperatures up to 135°C and delay times up to 2 ms.

title: Near-field contributions to cavity-mediated radiative heat transfer
abstract: Embedding materials in optical cavities has emerged as a powerful strategy for controlling their physical properties. In this context, increasing attention has been devoted to the thermal Purcell effect, which describes how the radiative heat transfer between a material and its photonic environ- ment can be modified by the electromagnetic boundary conditions imposed by the cavity. Here, we investigate near-field effects in cavity-mediated radiative heat transfer in planar cavities composed of realistic, dissipative gold mirrors, extending previous work that considered ideal mirrors. We iden- tify the conditions under which near-field effects lead to a substantial enhancement of heat transfer between the material and a photonic thermal bath relative to free space, owing to the strong modi- fication of the photonic local density of states by evanescent modes within the cavity. In particular, we find that radiative heat flow can be enhanced by several orders of magnitude in cavities ranging from nanometer to micrometer scales, depending on the absorber frequency and dipole orientation. These findings suggest that near-field effects may be relevant to polariton chemistry experiments and other systems operating within this cavity length-scale regime. Our results add to the idea that cavities can modify material properties not only by engineering vacuum fluctuations in the strong light-matter coupling regime, but also by controlling radiative dissipation and heat transfer.

title: Identification of carbon-related color centers in hBN by high-resolution ab initio photoluminescence modeling
abstract: Identification of optically active defects in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) remains challenging because different defect candidates can produce similar calculated photoluminescence (PL) lineshapes. Here, we demonstrate that force-constant embedding methodology can be extended to calculate high-resolution, vibrationally resolved PL lineshapes in the polar layered material hBN. Benchmarking against the carbon dimer defect, responsible for the 4.1 eV emission, we show that the methodology accurately reproduces the low-energy acoustic phonons and fine spectral features that are inaccessible when using direct supercell calculations. Applying the methodology to neutral carbon trimers ($\mathrm{C_2 C_B}$ and $\mathrm{C_2 C_N}$), we find that the calculated PL lineshape and excitation energy of $\mathrm{C_2 C_N}$ closely match the low-temperature spectrum of the emitter with a zero-phonon line at 1.54 eV. These results establish high-resolution phonon-sideband modeling as a powerful tool for discriminating among candidate defects in polar materials.

title: Polaritonic self-hybridized critical coupling by Brillouin zone folding induced quasi-bound states in the continuum in bulk WS2 metasurfaces
abstract: Maximizing the absorption of exciton-polaritons in transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) under critical coupling conditions is crucial for developing high-efficiency polariton-based photodetectors, solar cells, and perfect absorbers. Here, we propose a polaritonic critical self-hybridized coupling between Brillouin zone folding driven quasi-bound states in the continuum (BZF-QBIC) mode and A excitons in a bulk WS2 metasurface. This polaritonic critical coupling shows robust behavior with respect to the asymmetric parameters of the involved BZF-QBIC mode, in contrast to the asymmetry-sensitive conventional QBIC-based critical coupling. By changing the height of WS2 metasurfaces, we observe a typical anti-crossing behavior with a Rabi splitting of 246.5 meV. Moreover, the maximum absorption value of 0.5 for exciton-polaritons is achieved at the polaritonic critical coupling condition. The large population of excitons provided by bulk WS2 is essential for achieving polaritonic critical coupling and can further enhance polaritonic absorption. This work enables the realization of robust, high-absorption self-hybridized polaritonic critical coupling in TMDCs, and further expedite their applications in high-absorption low-dimensional polaritonic devices.

title: Non-Perturbative Bacterial Identification Directly From Solid Agar Plates Using Raman Micro-Spectroscopy and Machine Learning
abstract: Raman spectroscopy is a promising tool for microbial identification, yet its implementation in microbiology and clinical workflow is still restricted due to the accompanying additional preparation required to focus on microbial signals. Here, we demonstrate Raman-based bacterial identification directly from unopened, inverted agar plates, the same conditions used during incubation.

title: Structural optimization in TensErLEED using a parameter tree and R-factor gradients
abstract: Quantitative low-energy electron diffraction [LEED I ( V )] is a powerful method for surface-structure determination, based on a direct comparison of I ( V ) data between experiment and computations for a structure model. As the diffraction intensities I are highly sensitive to subtle structural changes, local structure optimization is essential for assessing the validity of a structure model and finding the best-fit structure. Even when using the tensor-LEED approximation—which accelerates optimization by applying a perturbative treatment of small deviations from a reference structure—the optimization process is computationally expensive. In the new tensor-LEED implementation presented in this work, the problem of surface-structure optimization is reformulated using a tree-based data structure, which helps to avoid redundant function evaluations. Intensities are computed on the fly, eliminating limitations of previous algorithms using grid-based search with precomputed values. This enables the use of state-of-the-art optimization algorithms. Implemented in Python with the JAX library, the method provides access to gradients of the R factor and supports execution on graphics processing units (GPUs). These developments reduce the computing time by more than an order of magnitude.

title: TMC-LewisGen: Automated Generation of Lewis-like Structures for Transition–Metal Complexes
abstract: Lewis structures constitute a foundational language in chemical education, mechanistic reasoning, synthesis, and modern cheminformatics. With the accelerating shift toward data-driven and AI-assisted molecular science, the ability to rapidly generate Lewis-like representations, including RDKit-parsable SMILES, has become essential for large-scale analysis and predictive modeling. While mature tools exist for organic molecules, transition-metal complexes (TMCs) remain systematically underserved owing to their inherently diverse coordination patterns.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Visualizing surface-reaction-driven chloride migration and cascading failure in sulfide solid electrolytes
abstract: Moisture instability of sulfide solid electrolytes limits practical use in all-solid-state batteries. Spatially resolving gas--solid reactions during moisture exposure remains challenging. Here, cryogenic four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (cryo-4D-STEM) maps nanoscale degradation in low- and high-Cl argyrodite electrolytes, Li\(_6\)PS\(_5\)Cl and Li\(_{5.5}\)PS\(_{4.5}\)Cl\(_{1.5}\). Li\(_6\)PS\(_5\)Cl undergoes predominantly surface-localized degradation that progressively extends inward, whereas Li\(_{5.5}\)PS\(_{4.5}\)Cl\(_{1.5}\) exhibits rapid interior amorphization accompanied by outward chloride redistribution. Density functional theory calculations indicate a lower chloride-migration barrier along the modeled pathway in the higher-Cl composition, while chloride removal and vacancy formation distort the PS\(_4^{3-}\) framework and may destabilize the lattice. Surface treatment suppresses detectable large-scale chloride segregation and improves moisture tolerance, retaining 99.9% of the capacity measured at the start of 0.33 C cycling after 150 cycles. These results identify chloride redistribution as a key process in degradation propagation and suggest a route toward moisture-tolerant solid-state batteries.

title: The Molecular Logic of Platelet-Activating Factor (PAF)
abstract: Platelet-activating factor (PAF) is a well-known if enigmatic lipid signal with important roles in inflammatory responses, allergic reactions, autoimmune diseases, and thrombotic cascades. Several lines of evidence suggest that our current model of PAF’s molecular mechanism is inadequate. This report describes a recontextualized model for PAF. The revised model embeds PAF in a plasmalogen-based molecular mechanism in which activation is a spontaneous chemical reaction triggered by environmental conditions that liberates a PAF receptor (PAF-R) agonist from a membrane-bound phospholipid. The active ligand subsequently undergoes a thermodynamically driven spontaneous rearrangement into an inactive isomer, a feature that controls response lifetime. The revised model is a molecule-autonomous set of transformations that create a response with spatial and temporal control. More generally the revised model’s congruence with a similar model for RORγt supports a picture in which plasmalogens form a part of the immune system that is separate from the cell-based innate and adaptive immune systems.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Photophysical and quenching principles governing advanced materials for fluorescence-based biosensing: mechanisms and analytical performance
abstract: Optical fluorescence biosensing has emerged as one of the most powerful strategies for ultrasensitive molecular detection, driven by rapid advances in fluorophore engineering, nanomaterial design, and signal-transduction architectures. At the core of these technologies lie fundamental excited-state processes, including fluorescence emission, Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET), photoinduced electron transfer (PET), and intramolecular charge transfer (ICT), that govern the generation, modulation, and detection of optical signals.

title: High-Frequency Mass Transfer Enabling Over-Limiting Currents in Porous Electrodes
abstract: Classical film theory predicts a finite diffusion-limited current at porous electrodes. However, over-limiting currents (OLCs), which exceed this limit, are often observed and have been attributed to surface charge, confinement, or electrokinetic effects. Here, we use a frequency-domain framework to identify a different mechanism governed by the time scale of concentration variation. For perfectly reactive interfaces, the spectral Sherwood number, a frequency-dependent dimensionless measure of interfacial mass transfer relative to molecular diffusion, grows as $\Shnd\simω^{1/2}$ at high frequency, while its phase approaches $π/4$. This response corresponds to the semi-infinite Warburg limit of the electrochemical impedance. A scaling analysis shows that the exponent and prefactor are determined by diffusion within a thin layer adjacent to the interface and are therefore independent of the global pore geometry. Numerical results for parallel plates, circular tubes, and twelve porous microstructures confirm this scaling. Geometry, flow strength, and flow direction affect the low-frequency response and crossover frequency, but not the asymptotic scaling in the high-frequency limit. This temporal route to OLCs requires neither surface charge nor confinement and could inform the design of systems for pulsed electrodeposition, mineral recovery and renewable-energy storage.

title: A Topological\-Geometrical Descriptor (TGD) for Scalable and Interpretable Modeling of Two\-Dimensional Carbon Networks
abstract: We introduce a compact Topological-Geometrical Descriptor (TGD) for planar two-dimensional carbon networks. Atomic coordinates are mapped to a periodic planar graph and represented through ring populations, topological-charge statistics, projected ring geometry, and dual-graph defect adjacency. The resulting modeling vector contains 19 physically interpretable features. We evaluate TGD on 120 published planar carbon allotropes using the DFT relative energy per atom with respect to graphene as the target. Repeated five-fold cross-validation with gradient boosting yields a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.0826 +/- 0.0138 eV/atom and R2 = 0.803 +/- 0.074. Under the same validation protocol, TGD gives a mean MAE of 0.0828 eV/atom, compared with 0.0929 eV/atom for a 203-feature Matminer representation. We further analyze 360 vacancy-defected graphene configurations spanning 12 vacancy concentrations from 2 to 24 percent. When entire vacancy concentrations are held out, TGD gives a pooled MAE of 0.269 eV/vacancy and R2 = 0.861, outperforming simple baselines based on vacancy concentration alone or non-hexagonal-ring fraction alone. Sensitivity tests show that the inferred edge sets are stable to moderate changes in the adaptive bond factor. Finally, the mean absolute topological charge is examined as a one-variable empirical surrogate for the allotrope dataset and is treated explicitly as dataset-specific rather than universal. These results show that TGD combines compact prediction with direct structural interpretation while making clear the present restriction to single-layer planar carbon networks.

title: Bulk superconductivity in quintuple-layer square-planar nickelate La6Ni5O12
abstract: Nickelate superconductors, sharing a similar electronic environment with cuprate superconductors, offer a promising platform for unraveling the mechanism of high-temperature superconductivity. However, the realization of superconductivity in these systems has so far been restricted to thin films or bulk samples under high-pressure. This limits the applicability of various experimental probes to study the mechanism of superconductivity, and hinders the potential application of the nickelate superconductors. Exploring bulk superconductivity at ambient pressure is therefore essential to understand its origin and enable broader experimental research. Here, we report the realization of bulk superconductivity at ambient-pressure in quintuple-layer square-planar (SP) nickelate La6Ni5O12. The SP phase is obtained by performing topotactic reaction on the quintuple-layer Ruddlesden-Popper (RP) compound La6Ni5O16. Optimized reduction condition endows La6Ni5O12 with a superconducting state that exhibits onset transition temperature of ~ 18 K, as verified by both zero resistance and diamagnetic shielding effect. Pronounced hysteresis loops revealed by magnetization and torque magnetometry demonstrate the occurrence of vortex pinning. Specific heat measurements on a polycrystalline pellet of La6Ni5O12 reveal a clear superconducting transition at ~18 K and a superconducting volume fraction of ~ 25%, which strongly supports the presence of bulk superconductivity. Our results establish an unprecedented bulk sample platform for investigating superconductivity in nickelates at ambient pressure, which paves the way for further experimental studies into the superconducting mechanism.

title: Predicting Unseen Scientific Interactions: Conditional Flow Models Hallucinate Non-Additive Effects
abstract: Conditional generative models are increasingly used for scientific prediction beyond the direct training support. Yet scientific questions often concern whether one intervention changes the effect of another. Such interactions can be of primary interest while explaining little of the total variation, allowing models to appear accurate overall without recovering the relevant scientific effect. It remains unclear how these models learn interactions and when these successfully extrapolate to unseen conditions. We therefore study interaction recovery in flow-matching models using a physiological time-series simulator, drug dose-response data, combinatorial cell perturbations, and molecular conformer generations, where we separate recovery from hallucinated interaction structure. In the controlled setting, individual effects are learned much earlier than interactions and models hallucinate interactions where none exist. Across settings, we find qualitatively different generalization problems, with successful prediction depending on whether condition structure continues from observed to held-out targets. When it does, interactions are recoverable. If not, models can generate plausible responses while missing the interaction. We furthermore find that hallucinations increase as targets become less identifiable, and that successful interaction recovery in output space can fail under nonlinear readouts. Finally, we show that aggregate fidelity metrics can conceal whether models learn and extrapolate interactions.

title: Generating Accurate Microstructures of Anisotropic Magnetorheological Elastomers
abstract: Anisotropic magnetorheological elastomers are magnetoactive smart materials whose complex magneto-mechanical behavior is strongly influenced by their underlying microstructure. Efficient and accurate multiscale simulations of these materials rely on small unit cells that reproduce the behavior of the real material. In this work, we present a framework for the generation and validation of such two-dimensional representative volume elements (RVEs) from a given microstructure image, assuming circular particles. The cells are generated through an optimization procedure where the two-point correlation function serves as a differentiable descriptor, while a minimum inter-particle distance is enforced as a constraint. To assess the equivalence of the generated cells, we compare their effective magneto-mechanical response with those of the reference microstructure. We demonstrate that the generated cells reproduce the reference response with high accuracy, also with substantially fewer particles. Consequently, the computational cost of subsequent multiscale simulations is reduced.

Identifying drugs associated with Alzheimer's disease risk using machine learning-assisted signal detection
abstract: BackgroundSeveral Alzheimer's disease (AD) clinical trials currently focus on drug repurposing. Machine learning (ML)-based pharmacoepidemiological approaches may help identify candidate drugs for trials.ObjectiveWe applied an ML-based signal detection method to identify drugs associated with AD risk.MethodsUsing Finnish nationwide register-based data, we defined drug exposure at both subgroup and drug substance levels according to the Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical classification.

title: AnDi-J: diffusion analysis of single-particle tracking data in Fiji
abstract: Characterizing how particles diffuse is key to understanding biology across scales, yet extracting the underlying physical properties typically requires specialized tools rarely accessible to biology labs. Here we introduce AnDi-J, a Fiji plugin combining classical estimators with state-of-the-art machine learning for single-trajectory analysis and segmentation, requiring minimal knowledge of stochastic processes. It extracts diffusion coefficients and anomalous exponents, classifies trajectories into diffusion models, and segments heterogeneous trajectories into diffusive states, through powerful, easy-to-use visualization tools. See more at https://github.com/gorkamunoz/andi-j .

title: Electron Counting by Design: Antiferromagnetic Ribbons Double as Charge Reservoirs to Stabilize Hypervalent Selenium and Tellurium Chains
abstract: Linear chains of hypervalently bonded chalcogen atoms are attractive building blocks for topological materials, but they almost always dimerize or modulate, and the few known examples are confined to actinide compounds. Here we show that Se, mixed Se/Te, and Te chains that are equidistant in their extended crystal structures are stabilized in a new Ibam structure type, Ba 2 Cu 2−x Fe 1+x Se 5−y Te y (y = 0 to 3.2), by combining a low reaction temperature (750 °C), aliovalent Cu/Fe mixing, and a geometric matching between the chains and ribbons of edge-sharing (Cu/Fe)Se 4 tetrahedra.

title: Validation Design Governs the Apparent Predictive Performance of Machine Learning for PLGA Drug Release
abstract: Reliable generalization is essential for machine-learning models intended to predict drug-release behavior across heterogeneous experimental settings. However, multi-study experimental data often contain closely related formulations generated under shared materials, processing conditions, release protocols, and laboratory practices, creating hidden dependencies between training and test data. Such dependencies can make model performance appear stronger than its ability to generalize to genuinely new experimental domains.

title: ddmo: A Compatible PySINDy Engine for Feature Optimization in Sparse Dynamical-System Discovery
abstract: Sparse equation discovery depends on the candidate functions, the treatment of noisy data, and the sparse regression procedure. These components are commonly configured independently, although their interactions directly affect model recovery. Our data-driven model optimizer ddmo uses PySINDy as its default sparse-regression backend and adds a modular, multiobjective optimization layer around it. Within one configurable search, users can vary parameters of prescribed candidate functions, regression settings, and the test functions and windows used to construct weak-form equations.

title: Investigating the Antioxidant Potential of Annona muricata Leaves- An in silico Assisted in vitro Approach
abstract: Annona muricata is traditionally used in the treatment of various infectious and chronic non – communicable diseases. The antioxidant activity of the leaves of A.muricata was assessed using DPPH scavenging assay. The DPPH radical scavenging potential was compared with the proven antioxidant, ascorbic acid. The result of the study showed that methanolic leaf extract of Annona muricata exhibited the greatest antioxidant activity than the other three extracting solvents used. title: Plasmonic Monolayer MoS 2 for Ultrathin Photoelectrodes in Neutral Water
abstract: Photoelectrochemical (PEC) electrodes can be used to create hydrogen to sustainably generate low-cost fuel and produce petrochemical feedstock. However, most semiconductors that drive the aqueous redox reactions in PEC devices cannot survive in neutral water, critical for widescale commercial production. Emerging, two-dimensional monolayer semiconductors can be electrochemically stable but generally do not capture enough sunlight to produce effective amounts of hydrogen.

title: How much of natural-product chemical space has a reference spectrum? An open audit of GNPS, MassBank and MoNA against COCONUT and LOTUS
abstract: Annotation of untargeted mass spectrometry data rests on reference MS/MS spectra, yet how much of documented natural-product (NP) chemistry actually has one has been asserted rather than measured. We present SPECGAP, an open, dependency-free engine that joins NP structure databases to spectral libraries on InChIKey identity and reports two quantities with explicit denominators: structural coverage, the share of reference structures with at least one experimental MS2 spectrum, and name-recoverability, the share of spectra whose declared compound name reconciles with the reference database.

title: Internally Polarized Covalent Organic Frameworks: A Design Strategy for Single-Component Photovoltaics
abstract: Molecular dipoles generate strong electric fields on the sub-nanometer scale, the very scale on which photogenerated excitons in organic semiconductors are bound. Harnessing such fields to drive charge generation throughout a photovoltaic material, however, has not been achieved. Realizing this would require ordering vast numbers of molecules throughout the bulk, which is precisely the structural control offered by covalent organic frameworks (COFs).

title: Multiscale modelling of acrylate networks
abstract: A systematic exploration of combining micro-to meso-to macro-scale models of crosslinking in three-dimensional polymer networks of Hexanediol Diacrylate (HDDA) is presented. Multi-scale modelling connecting realistic reaction kinetics from population balance (PB) models and network topology from molecular dynamics (MD) form the elements of the new modelling pipeline. Comparison of PB and MD predictions identify the initial radical concentration and model of initiation reactions as the principal source of discrepancy in species concentration profiles.

title: Old Drugs, New Targets: Multi-parameter computational prioritization of FDA‑approved, brain‑penetrant drugs as isoform‑selective GSK‑3β inhibitors for Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: Glycogen synthase kinase-3β (GSK-3β), a central regulator of tau phosphorylation and amyloid pathology, with its β isoform (GSK-3β) used as a main driver of the Alzheimer’s disease (AD) neurodegeneration. It is a validated therapeutic target in AD, yet no isoform-selective, brain penetrant inhibitors have reached clinical use. This paper screens 1000+ FDA-approved drugs by dual-isoform docking (GSK3α/β) and 8-seed redocking, prioritizing compounds by its α/β selectivity (G_select = G_GSK3A − G_GSK3B), CNS penetration, Hinge H-bonds, and pose plausibility.

title: Microstructure–Driven Degradation Mechanisms in High-Nickel NMC Cathodes for Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Mechanical degradation in high-nickel layered oxide cathodes is closely associated with anisotropic lattice-parameter changes during electrochemical cycling, yet how cathode microstructure size influences the resulting crystallographic deformation remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate two LiNi0.90Mn0.05Co0.05O2 (NMC955) cathodes with comparable secondary-particle sizes but different average grain sizes (1.0 and 0.5 µm).

title: Light and magnetism in the origin of extraterrestrial enantiomer excesses
abstract: Chiral compounds are composed of non-superimposable mirror-images, or enantiomers, typically designated as D- or L-isomers. The macromolecular structures of biopolymers share a critical trait known as homochirality: the exclusive presence of a single enantiomeric form within their organic building blocks. Understanding the origin of biological homochirality has been an active area of research for nearly two centuries. Our goal was to demonstrate the first de novo synthesis of individual sugar derivatives containing enantiomer excesses (ee), the precursor of homochirality.

title: A Redox-Switchable NIR II-to-NIR II Photoluminescent Vanadium(III/II) Redox Couple
abstract: Redoxluminochromic materials are useful for switchable optoelectronic devices that change the emission properties upon a redox stimulus. Typically, ON/OFF switches are realized, while materials with redox-induced changes of emission color are exceedingly rare. Here, we report a near-infrared II emissive vanadium(III) chromophore [V(tpe)2]3+ with an emission band peaking at 1110 nm. Its detailed photophysical properties including (ultrafast and long) excited state dynamics are elucidated by variabletemperature fs-ns transient absorption spectroscopy and luminescence spectroscopy.

title: Charge Donated by the Framework, Reactivity Expressed at the Metal: Tetrathiafulvalene-Programmed Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia
abstract: The decisive challenge in nitrate-to-ammonia electrosynthesis is not simply supplying electrons, but ensuring that successive nitrogen intermediates remain chemically convertible. Here, we establish a molecular strategy that differentiates framework-derived electronic character from metal-directed reaction selectivity through TU-420, a crystalline covalent organic framework integrating electron-donating tetrathiafulvalene and electron-accepting, metal-coordinating bipyridine units.

title: Structural Order Reversed: Local and Average Structure Across the Ammonia Borane Phase Transition
abstract: Ammonia borane (NH3BH3) is a hydrogen rich molecular solid whose structural behaviour is governed by molecular orientation and N–H· · ·H–B dihydrogen interactions. Its temperature-dependent phase transition is conventionally described as an order–disorder transition from a disordered tetragonal phase to a more ordered orthorhombic phase. However, this description does not fully capture the underlying local structure.

title: The eventful journey of a ligand in and out of the binding site
abstract: The route a ligand follows to reach and leave a protein binding site typically involves complex molecular mechanisms that shape its efficacy as a biologically active compound. These mechanisms are reflected in the binding and unbinding kinetics, which often predict biological activity better than binding affinity alone, yet their calculation remains a bottleneck in ligand characterization.

title: Crystallographic Visualization of Cooperative Molecular Motion Underlying the Photomechanical Response of a Diarylethene Crystal
abstract: Photomechanical molecular crystals convert molecular-scale photochemical reactions into macroscopic mechanical motion, yet how local structural changes develop into collective crystal deformation remains poorly understood. Here, we directly track the conversiondependent molecular motions underlying the photomechanical response of a diarylethene crystal, DAE-Et, by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Polarization-selective photoirradiation enabled the preparation of a series of photoreacted single crystals at different conversion levels while maintaining single crystallinity.

title: PolyNet: A Python Package for Polymer Informatics
abstract: Polymers are used in a wide range of industries for diverse applications but formulating them to attain desired properties remains a challenging task. Polymer informatics has emerged as a powerful approach for the rational design of materials. Here, we present PolyNet, an open-source Python package that provides an end-to-end workflow for polymer informatics. PolyNet: 1) reads and validates datasets of polymer properties, including the monomer structures and their molar ratios; 2) creates vector- and graph-based representations of the polymers; 3) trains and optimises traditional machine…

title: UPSTREAM: evidence-led, ledgered contribution to open metabolomics software, and what a corpus-wide name screen of MassBank found
abstract: Metabolomics depends on a small set of open projects—spectral libraries such as MassBank and GNPS, and processing software such as matchms and the RforMassSpectrometry packages—maintained largely by volunteers. Outside contributions can strengthen them or consume their maintainers’ time, and claims about how much someone has contributed are rarely verifiable. We describe UPSTREAM, a program that makes both problems explicit: every contribution must start from reproducible evidence and pass a ten-rule protocol, and the program’s headline count is computed from GitHub as merged pull requests…

title: Light-driven metal-free thiocarbonyl – olefin metathesis: a general route to sterically hindered alkenes
abstract: Highly substituted olefins are attractive scaffolds for molecular machines, optical materials and medicinal chemistry, whilst also serving as valuable intermediates in organic synthesis. However, their efficient and general preparation remains challenging, particularly in light of sustainability requirements. Here, we report a metal-free photochemical thiocarbonyl – olefin metathesis that provides access to a broad range of tri- and tetra-substituted alkenes, where light irradiation promotes both the regioselective formation and subsequent fragmentation of thietane intermediates.

title: Relativistic Bond Reconstruction in Chemical Bonding: An Information Dynamics Perspective on the CBi− Molecular Ion
abstract: In July 2026, the team of Lai-Sheng Wang at Brown University reported a landmark experimental observation in Science: the first direct spectroscopic evidence for the relativistic breakdown of the classical triple-bond picture in the CBi− molecular ion. Here we reinterpret this discovery through the lens of information dynamics—a framework that distinguishes between “real space” (wavefunctions and electron densities, where traditional quantum chemistry operates) and “virtual space” (defined here as the symmetry-rule manifold that organizes how real-space observables behave).

title: Linear inductive bias boosts extrapolative molecular discovery by Bayesian active learning in the small-data limit
abstract: Bayesian active learning is widely used for molecular discovery, yet surrogate selection remains challenging when scarce initial data must guide the search beyond the observed property range. Here we benchmark diverse Gaussian process (GP) configurations across ten small-molecule and polymer datasets, focusing on the extrapolative regime where the initial labeled samples are drawn exclusively from below the median of the target property distribution.

title: Development and Evaluation of a Low-Cost Bio-Adsorptive Filter Insert (DrainGuard) for Stormwater Microplastic Remediation
abstract: Sub-millimeter microplastics (100–300 μm) in urban stormwater runoff represent a significant, unaddressed pathway for aquatic pollution. Conventional catch basins and physical interception methods lack the retention efficiency required to capture fine polyolefin fragments during high-velocity first-flush events. This study presents DrainGuard, a modular, decentralized storm drain filter insert utilizing a stratified bio-adsorptive matrix composed of biogenic cockleshell sand and agricultural coconut coir.

title: Resilience and regime change in refining margins: evidence from cointegration, Markov chains, and topological data analysis
abstract: This paper analyses the 3:2:1 crack spread over 20 years (2006 to 2025) using three independent methods: Engle-Granger cointegration, Markov chain regime modelling, and persistent homology applied to Takens delay embeddings. The data are publicly available EIA spot prices obtained via the FRED database. The objective is to determine whether the long-run equilibrium relationship between crude oil and refined product prices has survived the structural shocks of the last decade: the oil price collapse of 2014-2016, the COVID-19 pandemic, the war in Ukraine, and the addition of new refining…

title: Identification of Readily Accessible Manganese Catalysts Enables Multi-gram Scale Enantioselective γ-C(sp 3 )‒H Lactonization of Carboxylic Acids
abstract: Selective C‒H bond functionalization is a powerful tool to access complex molecules within a minimal number of synthetic steps, but its applicability on a large scale is often hampered by the requirement of harsh reaction conditions and costly catalysts. Among the existing C‒H bond functionalization portfolio, carboxylic acid directed C‒H lactonization has emerged as a particularly valuable transformation since it provides access to synthetically versatile lactone products from readily available carboxylic acids.

title: DeNoMAP: An Interactive Web Application for Multi-Criteria Prioritization of De Novo Designed Compounds
abstract: De novo molecular generation is increasingly used in drug discovery, yet deciding which generated structures merit follow-up remains difficult, because established benchmarking metrics primarily characterize generative models rather than individual compounds. We present DeNoMAP, a general multi-criteria prioritization framework implemented as an interactive, open-access web application, which positions de novo-generated molecules in a normalized three-dimensional space defined by novelty, synthesizability and drug-likeness.

title: An experimentally-validated principle for selectivity in endergonic reactions
abstract: Selectivity between competing thermal reactions is, by textbook account, set either by the relative free energies of the products (thermodynamic control) or by those of the transition states leading to them (kinetic control). Neither principle applies to endergonic reactions: a non-equilibrium product concentration is maintained at the expense of an energy source, with species forming and decomposing simultaneously.

title: Hg(II) Coordination in Human Thioredoxin Reductase 1: Molecular Insights into Mercury Toxicity
abstract: Thioredoxin reductase 1 (TrxR1) is an essential selenoprotein oxidoreductase and a sensitive molecular target of mercury, but the coordination chemistry underlying its inhibition by inorganic Hg(II) remains unknown. We use complementary Hg LIII-edge and Se K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), high-energy-resolution fluorescence-detected XAS (HERFDXAS), and density functional theory (DFT) to determine the Hg(II) coordination environment in inhibited human TrxR1.

title: A Highly Stable Cyclic (Amino)(Aryl)Nitrenium Radical Dication Exhibiting Temperature-Dependent Radical Bistability Maruti Suryavansi,a Manas Khatua,b,d Bappaditya Goswami,c Apurba Kumar Pal,a Subhas Samanta,*d and K. Geetharani*
abstract: Development of air- and thermally stable organic radicals remains challenging due to the highly transient nature of the free radicals. Herein, we present a strategy for isolating a highly stable N-heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs) stabilized cyclic (amino)(aryl)nitrenium (CAArN) radical. This is the first example of a CAArN radical isolated in the solid state, and its identity has been confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and various spectroscopic studies.

title: Machine Learning Prediction of Subsequent Drug Release Trajectories using Early Release Information in PLGA Microparticles
abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-release behavior from PLGA microparticles may reduce the experimental effort required for formulation characterization, yet conventional prediction approaches rely primarily on static molecular and formulation descriptors and do not incorporate experimentally observed release behavior as it becomes available during an ongoing experiment. Here, we develop a machine-learning framework that integrates molecular and formulation descriptors with early-release measurements to predict subsequent drug-release trajectories from PLGA microparticles.

title: Arsenite (Trisenox) Bridges the Redox Centers of Thioredoxin Reductase
abstract: Arsenic trioxide (Trisenox) is an effective treatment for acute promyelocytic leukemia and is being explored for broader anticancer applications, yet our understanding of the molecular basis of its anticancer activity remains incomplete. Under physiological conditions arsenic trioxide forms arsenite, As(OH)3, which has been proposed to target the thioredoxin system. Here, we investigate the structural basis of arsenite interaction with mammalian thioredoxin reductase 1 (TrxR1, TXNRD1), a flavoenzyme selenoprotein essential for maintaining cellular redox homeostasis.

title: An Analytical Full-Dimensional Potential Energy Surface for the H + C3H8 Hydrogen Abstraction Reaction: Non-Equivalence of the Primary Hydrogens and Variational Transition State Theory Kinetics
abstract: A new analytical full-dimensional potential energy surface, PES-2026, is reported for the gas-phase hydrogen abstraction reaction H + C3H8 → H2 + C3H7. It is built within the valence bond–molecular mechanics, VB-MM, framework and depends on 72 parameters, 65 of which were optimized against a focal-point CBS benchmark and against UMP2/cc-pVTZ geometries, harmonic frequencies and reaction paths.

title: Balancing Plasmonic Response and CO2 Activation in Au–Cu/TiO2 Hybrid Photocatalysts via Alloy Composition Control
abstract: Plasmonic metal–semiconductor hybrid catalysts offer a versatile platform for solar-driven CO2 photoreduction by integrating efficient light harvesting with catalytic activation. Here, Au–Cu/TiO2 hybrid photocatalysts are developed as a model system to elucidate the role of plasmonic excitation and surface chemistry in governing CO2 reduction activity and selectivity. Alloyed Au–Cu nanorods with controlled Cu incorporation were synthesized and assembled with TiO2 nanoparticles, enabling systematic modulation of the Au/Cu ratio while maintaining constant metal and semiconductor loadings.

title: Metal-Organic Framework Shells Limit the Intracellular Collapse of AC Hysteresis in Magnetite Nanocubes
abstract: Intracellular confinement suppresses the dynamic magnetic losses of nanoparticles after uptake, limiting their efficacy under alternating magnetic fields (AMF). A crystalline metal-organic framework (MOF) shell limits this collapse by enforcing a minimum interparticle spacing that restricts the dipolar coupling imposed by endosomal packing. A conformal UiO-66 shell about 9 nm thick grows directly on poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG)-silane-stabilized Fe3O4 nanocubes at room temperature without N,N- dimethylformamide, giving single-core nanocomposites.

title: Heterotypic Imine Cross-links Reshape Phase Behavior and Relaxations in Polystyrene/Poly(ethylene glycol) Vitrimer Blends
abstract: Converting an immiscible polymer blend into a vitrimer is a powerful strategy for enhancing miscibility while still preserving viscoelasticity. In vitrimer blends, the chains bear dynamic covalent cross-links that undergo associative exchange – new bonds form before old bonds break, permitting the blend to maintain both network connectivity and topological fluidity. Recent studies have demonstrated that vitrimer blend phase behavior results from competition between homotypic cross-links between identical polymers and heterotypic cross-links between dissimilar species.

title: BOTREG and BAER: Source Selection Determines Whether Botanical Substitution Is Visible in the US Regulatory Record
abstract: Botanical substitution, the sale of one plant labeled as another, is a recognized hazard in dietary supplements, yet it is unclear how much of it the public regulatory record reveals. We introduce BOTREG, an open package that retrieves five US regulatory sources with guards against three silent failure modes, and BAER, the Botanical Adulteration Event Record derived from it. A production run screened 247,005 records (2004–2026) from openFDA food and drug enforcement, the CFSAN Adverse Event Reporting System (CAERS), the California Proposition 65 register, and FDA alerts and advisories.

title: Deactivation of SrTiO3 slurry and model photocatalysts during overall water splitting: Impact of Sr leaching on stability
abstract: Photocatalytic hydrogen evolution has been investigated for over five decades as a potential route to sustainable hydrogen production. SrTiO 3 (STO) is a benchmark photocatalyst because its band-edge positions enable overall water splitting. However, rapid charge-carrier recombination and sluggish interfacial redox kinetics limit light-to-product conversion efficiency, requiring suitable reduction and oxidation cocatalysts. While extensive research has addressed the activity and stability of cocatalysts, the stability of STO itself under reaction conditions has received less attention.

title: Helium Inclusion in a Mixed-Anion Framework Under Pressure: Discovery of Tetragonal BaFClHe and the Diamond Anvil Cell Sensor Paradox
abstract: Helium has the highest ionization potential among all elements (24.59 eV) and is notoriously chemically inert. Here, utilizing density functional theory (DFT-PBE-PAW) and density functional perturbation theory (DFPT), we report the discovery of a stable quaternary helium insertion compound in a mixed-anion matrix, BaFClHe, synthesized under moderate pressures of 35 GPa. In the tetragonal matlockite-derived framework (𝑃 4 𝑛𝑚𝑚, 𝑍 = 2), neutral helium atoms reside in square antiprismatic cavities (2𝑏 sites) without covalent charge transfer (𝑞 = +0.0395𝑒, 1𝑠1.962𝑝0.00).

title: Galvanic Coupling Links Heterogeneous and Molecular Palladium Catalysis in Aerobic Alcohol Oxidation
abstract: Thermochemical catalytic reactions often consist of coupled electrochemical half-reactions, which can even serve to generate the active catalyst itself. Here we show that oxygen reduction on heterogeneous palladium drives corrosion of Pd through galvanic coupling: oxygen reduction consumes the electrons released by oxidation of Pd(0) on the same catalyst, while the soluble Pd(II) forms a homogeneous complex which facilitates benzyl alcohol oxidation.

title: When Does MMLCT Emerge? The Role of Crystal Packing in the Photophysics of Pt(II) Polymorphs
abstract: Aggregation-induced metal-metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MMLCT) is widely used to rationalize the red-shifted and broadened emission observed in Pt(II) complexes. However, the underlying mechanism of MMLCT formation and its exact relationship with photoluminescence remain poorly understood. Polymorphism provides an ideal platform to isolate aggregation effects from molecular structural changes, because the same molecule can pack into different packing arrangements leading to strikingly different photophysical properties.

title: Steroid Thioesters to Target Golgi Apparatus
abstract: Despite Golgi apparatus plays a central role in lipid and protein trafficking, the biomedical potential of Golgitargeting supramolecular assemblies remains underexplored. While recent studies showed that peptide thioesters localize to the Golgi, it is unclear whether steroid thioesters can exhibit similar targeting behavior. Here, we designed and synthesized steroid-based thioesters by conjugating a thioester group and an NBD fluorophore to bile acids (BAs).

title: Mechanistic characterization of a bacterial terpene synthase that bifurcates to produce both 6/10- and 5/11-bicyclic diterpenes
abstract: The mechanism of the bacterial diterpene synthase ChtS from Chitinophaga japonensis was investigated. ChtS was found to produce two major diterpenes, 5/11-bicyclic chitino-2,5,9-triene (11) and the previously uncharacterized 6/10-bicyclic chitinoeunicellene (12). Deuterium labeling experiments, site-directed mutagenesis, and isolation of minor products cembrene C (13), cembrene A (14), and chitinol (15) support initial 1,14-cyclization, two sequential 1,2-hydride shifts, prior to bifurcation to 11 or 12, ultimately retaining the E-configured C-2/C-3 alkene.

title: Machine-learned interatomic potentials for battery materials: from fundamental methodology to emerging applications in electrodes, electrolytes, and interfaces
abstract: The rapid expansion of battery technologies beyond conventional lithium-ion systems has created an urgent demand for predictive, atomistic-scale simulation tools capable of addressing increasingly complex materials and interfaces. While first-principles calculations have played a central role in elucidating fundamental properties such as redox potentials, phase stability, and ion diffusion, its computational cost severely limits accessible system sizes and timescales.

title: On-Surface Synthesis of a Low Bandgap Cyclopenta[ c , d ]azulene-Based Polymer
abstract: Nonbenzenoid topologies offer a compelling strategy to tailor the electronic properties of low-dimensional carbon materials. Here, we report the on-surface synthesis of a nonalternant polymer incorporating a [7–5–5] cyclopenta[c,d]azulene (CPA) motif on Au(111) via thermally induced Ullmann coupling. Bond-resolved scanning tunneling microscopy confirms the robustness of the [7–5–5] framework. Scanning tunneling spectroscopy, together with dI/dV mapping supported by density functional theory calculations, reveals a remarkable narrow polymeric bandgap of 1.5 eV. The electronic structure is governed by the intramolecular charge transfer from the heptagonal ring to the adjacent fused pentagonal rings, resulting in a pronounced dipole moment despite being composed exclusively of carbon and hydrogen. Aromaticity analyses indicate the coexistence of locally aromatic and slightly antiaromatic regions, highlighting the intrinsic electronic frustration associated with the nonalternant topology. These findings demonstrate how the controlled incorporation of [7–5–5] motifs enables the rational bandgap engineering in carbon-based polymers and expands the scope of nonbenzenoid design in on-surface synthesis.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: PDI-Spot: A Robust Representation Learning Framework for Identifying Energetic Hotspots in Protein–DNA Complexes
abstract: The binding affinity of protein–DNA complexes is concentrated within a subset of interface residues, called “hotspots”, which are critical for maintaining stable interactions. Therefore, identifying these energetic anchors is essential for elaborating on how mutations disrupt transcriptional regulation and for identifying druggable regions within disease-associated interfaces. In this study, we introduce our novel prediction model, PDI-Spot, that leverages representation learning to capture the complex features of protein–DNA interfaces. Unlike traditional methods that rely on limited, handcrafted descriptors, PDI-Spot extracts high-dimensional, structure- and sequence-driven representations to achieve better predictive performance. We trained the PDI-Spot model on a curated protein–DNA complex data set and rigorously validated its performance on an independent test set to ensure generalizability across different structural families. Following the extraction of residue-level embeddings, an optimal feature set was identified through a combined approach of minimum redundancy maximum relevance and multilayer perceptron architectures. By training a neural network on the optimal feature set, we developed a robust predictive framework for hotspot identification. On an independent test set, PDI-Spot achieved an AUROC of 0.809, an F1-score of 0.667, and a Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.625. We also verified via permutation tests that PDI-Spot captures biologically meaningful patterns beyond random chance. PDI-Spot consistently demonstrates competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods, providing a reliable model for mapping the energetic landscapes of protein–DNA interfaces. The source code and pretrained models are publicly available at https://github.com/ebsrn0/pdi-spot.git.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Bridging the Markush Gap in Optical Chemical Structure Recognition via a CLIP-Derived Visual Backbone and Synthetic Data Generation
abstract: The rapidly growing chemical literature contains invaluable information for pharmaceutical research and molecular biology, yet manual extraction on a large scale is increasingly impractical. Optical chemical structure recognition (OCSR), which converts molecular depictions into machine-readable representations, provides a key route toward automated chemical information extraction.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: LNP Delivery of Prime Editors Enables Durable Correction of PAH R408W in Phenylketonuria Models
abstract: Phenylketonuria (PKU) is a monogenic metabolic disorder caused by mutations in the phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH) gene, the most common of which is c.1222C>T (p.R408W). Current treatment options, including dietary restriction and enzyme substitution, can be effective but are often challenging for patients to maintain and do not address the underlying genetic defect. Gene editing represents a compelling one-time treatment approach for PKU. Herein, we demonstrate mRNA:LNP-mediated delivery of prime editors that enable therapeutically-relevant levels of correction of the R408W mutation in both in vitro and in vivo model systems. Further, we found that co-delivery of the DNA repair modulator RAD18 and engineering of the prime editor protein, enabled 2-fold and 3-fold increases in prime editing relative to PE3 respectively, resulting in ~50% correction efficiency in a humanized PKU mouse model. Collectively, this work identifies novel potential approaches to enhancing prime editing and establishes LNP-delivered prime editing as a mutation-specific, non-viral therapeutic strategy for PKU, as well as providing a framework for extending prime editing to other inherited liver diseases.

title: Group Theory-Guided Orbital Symmetry Engineering of cis -Quinacridone: From Symmetry-Forbidden to Dipole-Allowed Transitions for Efficient Narrowband Emissions
abstract: Although group theory is widely used to analyze symmetry and electronic transition selection rules in condensed matter physics and coordination chemistry, its use as a predictive design tool for organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) remains largely unexplored. This is particularly important for highly symmetric emitters, where orbital-symmetry constraints can render the lowest-energy transition symmetry-forbidden.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: PFOS exposure and periodontitis from adolescent burden to genetic and multiomics evidence
abstract: Periodontitis can develop early in life and may be influenced by persistent environmental exposures. We integrated Global Burden of Disease 2021 data, Mendelian randomization, transcriptomics, machine learning, immune profiling, single-cell analysis, molecular modeling, and in vitro validation to investigate links between perfluorooctane sulfonate exposure and periodontitis. Periodontal disease burden remained substantial among individuals aged 5-20 years and varied across sociodemographic strata. Genetically predicted PFOS exposure was associated with increased periodontitis risk by inverse-variance weighted Mendelian randomization. Multi-omics analyses identified 151 shared targets enriched in immune-inflammatory pathways and prioritized a ten-gene signature with strong diagnostic discrimination. Single-cell analysis implicated migration inhibitory factor (MIF)-centered immune communication, whereas molecular modeling supported stable PFOS-STK17B interactions. PFOS exposure in human gingival fibroblasts increased expression of the ten prioritized genes. These findings connect population burden with genetic, molecular, and experimental evidence supporting immune-inflammatory mechanisms linking PFOS exposure to periodontitis.

title: Catalytic Asymmetric 1,6-Diene Cyclization via Designed Carbocationic 5- and 6- exo Pathways
abstract: Catalytic asymmetric electrophilic alkene functionalization provides a powerful strategy for the construction of complex chiral molecules. Despite significant progress in this field, the asymmetric functionalization of alkenes promoted by an electrophilic carbon species via an exo-cyclization mode remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a solution to this challenge: alkenes can undergo designed 5-exo- and 6-exo-carbocationic cyclizations to generate optically pure, complex chiral compounds with high enantio- and diastereoselectivities.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Evidence for multi-Li+ clustering in lithium-ion battery electrolytes
abstract: In lithium-ion batteries, the bulk solvation structure of the electrolyte is a major determinant of the physical and electrochemical properties of the cell, for example, conductivity, viscosity, salt dissociation and subsequent reactivity, the electrochemical stability window (and thus solid electrolyte interphase formation), and the composition of the electrochemical double layer1-3. However, elucidation of this structure at an atomic level of detail has been challenging to accomplish via a purely experimental approach. Here we combine machine-learning-enabled atomistic simulations4-16, nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, electrochemical data3,17-20 and quantum-chemical calculations to reveal previously unstudied multi-Li+ complexes without bound anions that are uniquely facile for reduction. This insight explains the success of empirically chosen ethylene-carbonate-containing solvent mixtures and provides a foundation for the rational design of improved electrolytes. Furthermore, our machine-learning force-field-based lithium-ion-battery electrolyte simulations accurately reproduce a wide range of condensed-phase experiments3,21-24, despite being parameterized to only quantum-chemical gas-phase cluster calculations, and hence provide a compelling demonstration that machine-learning force-field-based models developed from first principles can robustly represent a complex chemical system to atomic resolution.

title: Prenatal fipronil sulfone exposure is associated with altered fetal liver-function biomarkers: Evidence integrating epidemiology, network toxicology, and molecular docking
abstract: Fipronil and its metabolites (FPM) are widely detected in environmental and biological matrices, but human evidence of developmental hepatotoxicity remains scarce. We quantified six fipronil-related compounds, five liver-function biomarkers, and four inflammatory cytokines in umbilical cord serum from 187 neonates. Fipronil sulfone was detected in all samples (median: 101.6 pg/mL). In covariate-adjusted linear models, each 10-fold increase in fipronil sulfone was associated with higher alanine aminotransferase (ALT) [β = 3.73, 95% CI: (1.58-5.88)], aspartate aminotransferase (AST) [β = 13.13, 95% CI: (2.15-24.12)], gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) [β = 51.50, 95% CI: (3.74-99.25)], and alkaline phosphatase (ALP) [β = 93.52, 95% CI: (44.61-142.44)]. The associations with ALT and ALP remained statistically significant after FDR correction. Bayesian kernel machine regression and machine-learning models consistently prioritized fipronil sulfone as an important mixture component associated with these biomarkers. Exploratory BBMD analysis estimated benchmark concentrations associated with a 10% change in liver-function biomarkers. Mediation analyses indicated that interleukin-1β partially mediated the associations with ALT and AST (16.25% and 19.75%, respectively), whereas tumor necrosis factor-α mediated the associations with ALT, AST, and ALP (11.21%-20.91%). Network toxicology highlighted inflammatory, oxidative-stress, PI3K-Akt, MAPK, and TNF signaling pathways, and molecular docking predicted favorable binding of fipronil sulfone to TNF, ALB, and INS. These findings associate cord-serum fipronil sulfone concentrations with altered cord-serum liver biomarkers and identify inflammatory signaling as a potential intermediate pathway. Longitudinal and experimental studies are needed to confirm temporality and biological causation.

title: scikit-fingerprints : A Python Library for Scikit-Learn-Compatible Molecular Fingerprints and Chemoinformatics
abstract: We present scikit-fingerprints, a comprehensive, fully scikit-learn-compatible library for molecular machine learning in Python, based on RDKit. Molecular fingerprints and related functionalities are workhorses of chemoinformatics, yet the widely used open-source frameworks are not compatible with the wider Python machine-learning ecosystem based on scikit-learn conventions. scikit-fingerprints closes this gap, bringing molecular fingerprints, molecular filters, similarity and distance measures, applicability domain estimation, data-splitting strategies, and more under a single familiar interface. Scikit-learn compatibility means that an entire chemoinformatics workflow, from a raw SMILES string to a deployable model, can be assembled from composable building blocks and can reuse the mature tooling of the surrounding ecosystem. The underlying RDKit code makes the library familiar and extensible for custom chemoinformatics use cases. We put a strong focus on unified interfaces, ease of use, computational efficiency, customization, and extensibility. scikit-fingerprints makes molecular machine learning faster to prototype, easier to reproduce, and simpler to deploy.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: e MolFrag 2 and e Synth 2: Sound Fragment-Based Molecular Decomposition and Reconstruction
abstract: We present eMolFrag2 and eSynth2, enhanced successors to eMolFrag and eSynth for fragment-based molecular decomposition and reconstruction. eMolFrag2 is a complete reimplementation of eMolFrag in Python, using RDKit and graph-based molecular representations to preserve connectivity, identify free atoms, combine adjacent linkers, and avoid aromaticity ambiguities that impair downstream reconstruction. eSynth2 generalizes fragment recombination by removing hard-coded molecular-property filters, supporting multiple bonds to a single brick atom, and adding a targeted reconstruction mode for soundness validation. Across 36,534 nonredundant DUD-E active compounds, the eMolFrag2 → eSynth2 workflow reconstructed every input molecule exactly (Tanimoto coefficient, TC = 1.0), whereas the original eMolFrag→ eSynth workflow reconstructed 51 of the 100 molecules in a benchmark subset. The upgraded workflow also produced broader recombinant chemical spaces, including higher entropy in a four-molecule diversity analysis (2.78 versus 2.70). Both tools are open-source, platform-agnostic, and available for academic and commercial use.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Unfolding of the disease-linked bank vole prion protein E200K in the context of PrPSc propagation
abstract: The elucidation of the atomistic structure of PrPSc has, disappointingly, not revealed the mechanism underlying prion propagation. This is because PrPSc has been shown to be a standard amyloid, and as such, it can only template a polypeptide chain that is unfolded. Therefore, while PrPSc can easily template the disordered ~90-120 domain of an incoming PrPC molecule, it does not have any obvious capacity to template its ~121-231 folded domain (FD). The FD needs to accommodate into the ~121-230 PrPSc surface, an inert "Procrustean bed". We have recently proposed that unfolding of the FD is a prerequisite for its conversion to the PrPSc conformation and using experimental and computational methods identified the likely early events of such process using bank vole (BV)PrP(90-231) as our working model. We concluded that a key early event is the destabilization of the short {beta}1-{beta}2 assembly, and that the segment contiguous to the disordered tail, ~121-140, encompassing {beta}1 and its adjacent coils, is the most likely region to unfold first. In the present study we applied the same methodology to the disease-related PrP mutant E200K. E200K is the most prevalent mutation leading to familial prion disease in humans, yet the stability of its FD is only marginally lower compared to that of the protein with the wild type (wt) sequence. We, therefore, aimed at assessing whether the early unfolding events of BVPrPC(E200K) are similar or different to those of wtBVPrPC and whether such early unfolding route might provide insight into the extreme capacity of PrPC(E200K) to spontaneously generate PrPSc. It should be noted that generation and propagation of PrPSc are distinct phenomena, even though both are mechanistically related and dependent on conformational changes in PrPC. Our data show that early unfolding events of BVPrPC(E200K) are essentially similar to those of wt BVPrPC. However, interesting nuances exist.

title: Microcalorimetry reveals bacterial motility as an expensive trait during starvation
abstract: Quantifying the energetic costs of cellular traits is important to understand their evolutionary constraints and ecological function. However, direct measurements of energy expenditure of distinct traits are rare. Here, we present direct measurements of the power dissipation due to bacterial flagellar motility using microcalorimetry, based on measuring the power dissipation of a motile population and a non-motile mutant. For the single-flagellated marine bacterium \textit{Vibrio coralliilyticus}, we determined the power dissipated by motility in cultures to be 0.91 W/mL/OD.
