title: AI-ASSISTED NANOMEDICINE REVEALS SYSTEMIC IMMUNE IMPACT IN OVARIAN CANCER METASTASIS
abstract: Ovarian cancer, a gynecological malignancy, poses a significant challenge as researchers struggle to comprehend how tumor cells communicate with the immune system. Ovarian tumors contain both bulk cancer cells and cancer stem cells (CSCs), which are linked to chemoresistance, relapse, and immune escape. However, it remains unclear whether these two populations affect immune cells differently.

title: To Recover or Not to Recover: A Urinary Proteomic Perspective on Severe Acute Kidney Injury
abstract: Rationale & Objective Early prediction of renal non-recovery after acute kidney injury (AKI) could support risk-adapted follow-up and clinical decision-making. We evaluated whether a urinary fatty acid-binding protein 3 (FABP3)/apolipoprotein A-I (APOA1) ratio based on Total Protein Approach (TPA) quantification could discriminate renal recovery from non-recovery after severe AKI. Study Design Exploratory biomarker discovery study with outcome-blinded independent validation. Setting & Participants Critically ill adults with KDIGO stage 2 or 3 AKI.

title: Skill-guided agentic reasoning enables longitudinal synthesis of myeloma records at expert-level concordance
abstract: Patients with multiple myeloma accumulate hundreds of clinical documents over years of sequential therapy, and every treatment decision depends on synthesis across that history. Whether large language model-based systems can match expert agreement on this task, and where they fail, has not been established. On longitudinal records of 811 patients treated over 25 years (44,962 documents and 1,334,677 laboratory values), an agentic reasoning system guided by an indexed clinical skill library was compared against single-pass retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), iterative RAG, iterative RAG augmented with the same skill library, and full-context input on 469 expert-adjudicated patient-question pairs, with an exploratory cross-dataset evaluation on MIMIC-IV. The skill-guided agent exceeded the ceiling at which iterative RAG (75.7%) and full-context input (75.8%) converged, reaching 80.1% concordance, with its advantage widening on the most complex tasks (+11.2 percentage points) and longest records. Providing the same skill library to iterative RAG matched the agent in aggregate (79.0%) and on shorter records, whereas the agent retained a significant advantage on the longest records (+10.3 percentage points in the top decile, p = 0.017) and a numerical, non-significant advantage on the most complex questions (+5.4 percentage points). The aggregate error rate (12.2%) was comparable to expert disagreement (13.6%), but a higher proportion of system errors were clinically significant (57.8 versus 18.8%).

title: Grain-Size Dependence of Thermal and Electrical Properties in (Cr,Mo,Ta,V,W)C1-δ High-Entropy Carbide Ceramics
abstract: Thermal and electrical transport in high-entropy carbides can be influenced by grain-boundary scattering, but the relevant microstructural regime remains uncertain. Here, near-fully dense $(Cr,Mo,Ta,V,W)C_{1-δ}$ ceramics were densified by spark plasma sintering at 1750-1950 °C, producing average grain sizes from 9.3 $\pm$ 4.9 to 28.8 $\pm$ 15.3 $μ$m while retaining the rock-salt phase. Heat capacities were measured experimentally and estimated by the Neumann-Kopp law with the latter used to calculate thermal conductivity. Thermal conductivity values were in the range of 6.8-7.1 W $m^{-1}$ $K^{-1}$ at room temperature, but showed no systematic dependence on grain size within the investigated range. Room-temperature electrical resistivity values were in the range of 151.9 to 177.0 $μΩ$ cm and likewise showed no grain-size dependence. The electron contribution to room-temperature thermal conductivity was estimated to be approximately 58-68% of total thermal conductivity as estimated using the Wiedemann-Franz law and the theoretical Lorenz number. The results indicated that processing-induced grain coarsening did not produce clearly resolvable transport-property changes under the conditions investigated leading to the conclusion that intrinsic disorder and defect chemistry may exert stronger influences on properties.

title: Understanding the role of chromatin accessibility and compaction on loop extrusion dynamics
abstract: Loop extrusion by SMC complexes is a fundamental mechanism regulating the three-dimensional genome organization, but how these molecular motors navigate through the crowded, nucleosome-covered chromatin fiber remains an open question. Here, we develop a stochastic biophysical model of loop extrusion that explicitly couples motor stepping dynamics to chromatin accessibility and compaction. First, we systematically analyze the role of accessibility on its dynamics across homogeneous, periodic, and random roadblock positioning along chromatin. This comprehensive analysis reveals distinct dynamic regimes: phase-dependent kinetics in periodic arrays where motor step size aligns with obstacle spacing, and anomalous sub-linear progression in disordered environments due to rare but long-lived trapping events. Then, we contextualize our framework to nucleosome-like arrays. Our simulations reveal a non-intuitive dual role for nucleosomes: while they hinder extruder progression by blocking access to linker DNA, their high compaction packs more base pairs per physical distance, enabling larger genomic displacements per step. Strikingly, the resulting base-pair extrusion speed displays a non-monotonic dependence on nucleosome spacing, reaching a maximum at intermediate linker lengths (10-70 bp) that can exceed the speed on naked DNA. Finally, in support of this mechanism, analysis of yeast genomic data shows that a higher nucleosome occupancy between cohesin-associated regions correlates with stronger contact enrichment, consistent with compaction-enhanced extrusion efficiency in vivo. These findings establish chromatin architecture as a tunable regulator of loop extrusion, explaining the comparable speeds observed in vitro and in vivo and providing a quantitative framework for understanding how genome organization emerges from the interplay between motor kinetics and chromatin structure.

title: Archival data storage using DNA proximity graphs
abstract: DNA offers a promising medium for long-term archival data storage, but data-specific DNA synthesis remains costly. Here we introduce SPAN (Synthesis-free Proximity-graph Archiving in Nucleic acids), a synthesis-independent storage architecture in which information is written as a physical pattern and encoded in the spatial relationships of randomly barcoded DNA molecules. Barcodes are deposited onto an optically patterned surface, and an enzymatic reaction records neighboring barcode pairs. Sequencing these pairs produces a proximity graph from which the information is decoded. We demonstrate this principle by writing a 136-bit pattern using photolithography and recovering 90% of the bits. Our cost analysis estimates lower writing costs than any existing DNA storage method. Using established commercial optical writing technologies, we project a further five-order-of-magnitude cost reduction to below flash memory costs. Although readout is more expensive, this trade-off is attractive for deep archival storage, where information is written once and rarely, if ever, retrieved.

title: Computationally Guided Design of Facet-Defined Multielement Active Sites on Hexagonal Close-Packed High-Entropy-Alloy Nanosheets for Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution
abstract: Nonconventional hexagonal close-packed (HCP) high-entropy alloys (HEAs) provide distinct catalytic surfaces, but their synthesis with well-defined facets remains challenging, leaving facet-dependent multielement ensemble effects largely unexplored. Here, we report the computationally guided realization of atomically thin RuRhIrPtPd HEA nanosheets with predominantly exposed HCP {001} facets for the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Density functional theory (DFT) calculations identify HCP {001} as the most favorable facet over {100} and {110}, where near-thermoneutral hydrogen adsorption, narrow energy distribution, and balanced hydrogen/hydroxyl binding create an optimized alkaline HER landscape. Guided by this prediction, RuRhIrPtPd HEA atomic layers are epitaxially grown on HCP Ru nanosheets to maximize {001} exposure, with atomic-resolution electron microscopy and synchrotron X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) confirming atomically mixed HEA layers. Electrochemical measurements demonstrate that the {001}-faceted HEA nanosheets exhibit higher alkaline HER activity and durability than irregular-faceted nanocrystal counterparts and commercial Pt/C. Climbing-image nudged elastic band (CI-NEB) calculations, operando XAS, and CO-stripping measurements identify Ru-centered ensembles as favorable Volmer sites, showing the lowest water-dissociation barrier of 1.04 eV compared with 1.13–1.47 eV for other metal sites, while neighboring multimetallic sites balance hydrogen and hydroxyl adsorption. This work provides a structural blueprint for harnessing facet-defined multielement ensembles to design high-entropy electrocatalysts.

title: Quantifying electronic insulation of solid-electrolyte interphases through electrolyte decomposition kinetics
Titanium-Catalyzed Divergent Deoxycyclization for Synthesizing Semisaturated Nitrogen Heterocycles
abstract: Semisaturated nitrogen heterocycles, such as 3-pyrrolines and unsaturated azepanes, possess highly prized three-dimensional geometries for drug discovery. However, their divergent synthesis from simple, unactivated feedstocks remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a highly selective, titanium-catalyzed divergent radical deoxycyclization coupling of nitrosoarenes and 1,3-dienes.

title: Pd-Sensitized SnO2@WO3 Nanosheets via Cluster-Nucleus Coassembly: Enhanced Hydrogen Spillover for High-Efficiency H2 Sensing
abstract: The risk of hydrogen explosions in industrial and hydrogen energy facilities presents serious safety threats. An inherent trade-off between response magnitude and response/recovery kinetics plagues chemiresistive H2 sensors: monocomponent materials are incapable of concurrently realizing high-efficiency H2 activation and ultrafast gas-solid interfacial charge transfer/desorption. Herein, we synthesized SnO2@WO3 hexagonal nanosheets via hydrothermal cluster-nucleus coassembly and decorated them with Pd nanoparticles by wet-chemical reduction.

title: Understanding the Role of Band Bending and Surface Coordination in Steering Piezocatalytic In Situ H2O2 Evolution Routes
abstract: Piezocatalytic H2O2 production, employing water and oxygen as the raw materials, is emerging as a promising and viable alternative for in situ H2O2 evolution. However, the understanding of the structure–activity relationship of piezocatalysts still poses challenges, and the key factor steering the H2O2 evolution pathway also remains ambiguous. title: Spatial Separation of Metal–MOF Tuning Catalytic Selectivity in CO2 Hydrogenation and Methanol Partial Oxidation
abstract: Tuning the interactions between metal nanoparticles (NPs) and metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) is pivotal for selective catalysis, yet systematic regulation of metal–MOF spatial separation remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate that systematically regulating the metal–MOF separation enables controlled modulation of catalytic activity and reaction selectivity. A series of MOF-encapsulated Pt catalysts with adjusted Pt–MOF separations were designed and synthesized by varying the surface coverage of capping agents on Pt NPs.

title: Lewis Acid-Catalyzed Vinyl Transfer Using Vinylene Carbonate for Direct Synthesis of C2,C3-Unsubstituted Indoles
abstract: C2,C3-unsubstituted indoles are privileged scaffolds in medicinal chemistry, yet their direct assembly from simple C2 feedstocks remains a longstanding synthetic challenge. Herein, we report an example of Y(OTf)3-catalyzed C–H [3 + 2] annulation of anilines with vinylene carbonate, enabling direct access to structurally diverse parent indoles through a Lewis acid-catalyzed vinyl-transfer process.

title: Structural Basis for Angiotensin II Type I Receptor G Protein-biased Signaling
abstract: Biased agonism at the angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) offers a promising strategy for developing safer cardiovascular therapeutics. While beta-arrestin-biased agonism has been extensively investigated, G protein-biased signaling remains poorly understood. Here, we report structures of AT1R coupled to G protein and either the endogenous agonist angiotensin II (AngII) or the G protein-biased agonist TRV055. The ligands adopt similar overall poses, with coordinated rearrangements extending from the orthosteric pocket to the intracellular surface. The structures provide a detailed view of a TM7-centered microswitch network linking ligand recognition to G protein coupling. Functional analyses of peptide analogs identify the ligand's amino terminus as a key determinant of G protein bias, while mutagenesis of the microswitch network shifts AngII toward beta-arrestin-biased signaling and converts the G protein-biased agonist TRV055 into a beta-arrestin-biased ligand. These findings establish a framework for G protein-biased AT1R activation and provide mechanistic insight for the rational design of pathway-selective GPCR therapeutics.

title: A Pyridoxal 5′-Phosphate-Dependent Decarboxylative Mannich Reaction Initiates Construction of the Nonpeptidic Scaffold of Kaitocephalin
abstract: Kaitocephalin (KCP) is a fungal neuroactive natural product bearing a peptide-like yet nonpeptidic amino acid-derived scaffold in which amino acid-like units are connected by C–C bonds rather than peptide bonds. The enzymatic construction of this unusual scaffold has remained unresolved. Here, we identify KpbH as a pyridoxal 5′-phosphate (PLP)-dependent enzyme that couples pyrroline-5-carboxylate, generated from l-ornithine, with l-aspartate to form (2S,5R)-5-[(S)-2-amino-2-carboxyethyl]pyrrolidine-2-carboxylic acid (ACPCA), which corresponds to the nonpeptidic Ala–Pro substructure of KCP. D2O-labeling experiments showed enzyme-controlled, solvent-derived deuterium incorporation at C7 of ACPCA, supporting a decarboxylative Mannich-type mechanism. Feeding of a deuterium-enriched ACPCA-containing reaction mixture to the KCP-producing fungus Eupenicillium shearii resulted in deuterium incorporation into KCP, linking ACPCA to KCP biosynthesis. These results identify KpbH as the first native PLP-dependent enzyme that catalyzes an l-aspartate-dependent decarboxylative Mannich-type C–C bond-forming reaction and reveal a biosynthetic strategy for constructing a noncanonical amino acid-like C–C bond scaffold.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
